display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Building an inventory tracking system for the cannabis industry is extremely challenging—even harder for tech companies than for cannabis businesses themselves.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: 'Seed-to-sale' is a regulatory term (not technical) meaning: a state-mandated cannabis tracking system.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: It started in Colorado due to the Cole Memo—a U.S. Department of Justice policy.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Colorado implemented seed-to-sale tracking to show the federal government it could self-regulate and ensure transparency.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Over the past 14 years, cannabis tech has improved dramatically.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Early systems relied on manual data entry, had frequent errors, and lacked APIs to connect with state systems.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Today, third-party software vendors face two big challenges:\n1. Integrating with state traceability systems (like Metrc)\n2. Building in compliance safeguards for each state’s unique rules.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: If you're building software that connects to systems like Metrc—or planning to—this guide covers what you need to know.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Based on 9+ years of consulting with cannabis tech companies, here are the core topics you must understand:

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: 1. How supply chains are structured differently across states

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: 2. Key differences between inventory tracking, batch tracking, serialization, and tag management

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: 3. Critical compliance requirements during development

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: 4. How to properly integrate with Metrc and ERP systems

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: ⚠️ Warning: Many cannabis software vendors falsely claim to be 'ERP systems.'

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: According to Oracle, a true ERP manages: accounting, procurement, project management, risk, compliance, AND supply chain operations.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Most cannabis software only handles supply chain functions—not full ERP capabilities.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Every U.S. state with legal cannabis (medical or adult-use) has its own rules for how the supply chain operates.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: There are two main supply chain models:

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Model 1: Dual-License (Segregated) Supply Chain

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - At planting, each plant is labeled as either 'medical' or 'adult-use.'

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - That designation follows the product all the way to the final sale.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Businesses usually need two separate state licenses to operate both tracks.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Some states allow limited crossover, but workflows are highly state-specific.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Model 2: Single Supply Chain

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - All inventory is undifferentiated (can be sold as medical OR adult-use) from seed to retail.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - The final sale transaction determines whether it’s a medical or adult-use sale.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Caveats: purchase limits, product quantity, and THC content may still differ by customer type.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Often, only one business license is needed to produce for both markets.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: States also differ in how businesses can interact within the supply chain:

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Example: California

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Only licensed distributors can transport products.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Distributors must also handle lab testing (Certificate of Analysis or 'COA').

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Example: Michigan, Colorado, Massachusetts

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Cultivators and manufacturers can self-distribute their own products.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Lab testing typically happens within the cultivation or manufacturing facility—not at distribution.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Why this matters: Your software must enforce what’s legally allowed in each state.\nYou must understand the regulatory framework and licensing structure of every state you support.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Now, let’s clarify commonly confused tracking terms used in cannabis compliance:

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Core Tracking Identifiers and Batches:

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: • Metrc Package Tag: A state-issued barcode tracking a final packaged product.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: • Metrc Plant Tag: A state-issued tag tracking a live plant from cultivation.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: • Unique Identifier (UID): Regulatory term that usually just means 'Metrc tag'—states avoid naming Metrc directly in laws.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: • Harvest Batch: A group of the same cannabis strain, harvested at the same time, using identical growing methods.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: • Production Batch: A group of identical manufactured products (e.g., gummies, oil) made in one run with homogenized inputs and outputs.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: • Testing Lot: A sub-portion of a harvest batch sent for lab compliance testing.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: → Example: In Oklahoma, a 50-pound harvest must be split into five 10-pound testing lots because state law limits harvest batches to 10 lbs.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: → You can have multiple testing lots from a single harvest batch.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: → Tip: Say 'testing lot' (not 'test batch')—it better reflects it’s a subset of a larger batch.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: • SKU (Stock Keeping Unit): Identifies a specific product variant, often tied to a batch or individual unit.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: • UPC (Universal Product Code): Identifies a general product type across all batches (e.g., '100mg THC gummy pack').\n→ Can cause confusion in Metrc because it ignores batch differences.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: When building your software, you must handle these compliance requirements:

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: 1. Purchase Limits & Equivalencies

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Prevent the point-of-sale (POS) from overselling to a customer (which causes instant violations).

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Limits are based on either total weight purchased OR total THC content.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - States define 'equivalencies' differently (e.g., 1 gram of concentrate = 5 grams of flower).

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Your system must support weight-based, THC-based, and mixed-unit calculations (grams, mg, ounces).

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
div.span: 2. Tax Reporting

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Clarify: Who collects taxes? Who keeps records? Who enters tax codes into the POS?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Best practice: Let the retailer configure their own tax rules in your software.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Why? If your system auto-enters taxes and the retailer under-reports, YOU could face legal liability.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
div.span: 3. Testing & Recall Tracking

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Your system must collect and store Certificate of Analysis (COA) data.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Enable full product recalls by harvest batch, production batch, or testing lot.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
div.span: 4. Labeling Requirements

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Regulators inspect dispensaries to ensure labels don’t overlap.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - All required info (potency, ingredients, warnings) must be fully visible to the customer.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - Offer multiple label sizes so retailers can choose based on product packaging.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
div.span: - State rules are often unclear about who (brand vs. retailer) is responsible for label content—so build flexibility.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Metrc Integration Strategy:

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Do NOT try to support the entire supply chain across all states at once.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Instead: Pick a niche—e.g., cultivators, manufacturers, distributors, or retailers.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Master compliance for that segment in one or two states, then expand.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Building a fully compliant, full-supply-chain, multi-state system is nearly impossible—even after 9+ years, no vendor has truly achieved it.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Technically, Metrc’s API lets you send data to any state with just a few endpoints.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: But technical access ≠ compliance success.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Metrc accepts ANY data—even non-compliant entries. Your software must act as a 'safety net' with built-in regulatory checks.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Passing Metrc’s API certification only means you can send data—it does NOT mean you’re compliant with state law.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: True compliance requires deep safeguards for: labels, testing, purchase limits, taxes, and B2B transaction rules.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: ERP Integration Best Practice:

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Use a cannabis-specific system for all 'plant-touching' operations (growing, processing, selling).

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: This system should integrate DIRECTLY with Metrc.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: It should also push financial and operational data into a true ERP (like NetSuite or SAP) for business-wide reporting.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: 🚫 Never create a 'telephone game' where: ERP → Cannabis Software → Metrc.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: This multi-hop integration causes API errors, data mismatches, and compliance risks for your clients.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: This is just the tip of the iceberg—compliant cannabis software requires deep knowledge of workflows, regulations, and integration patterns.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: With focused guidance (e.g., 10 hours of consultation), you can build a roadmap to develop adaptable software that works across any state’s rules—accelerating your market entry and reducing risk.
